Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

swe-marathon · access terms: The SWE-Marathon creator README declares Apache 2.0 but describes its roughly 800 GB trajectory bucket as public while also asking users to request S3 credentials for downloading logs.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next12.swe-marathon.access.v2

  • The contradictory access description remains unresolved; no credentials, outreach or bulk log download was attempted. Code/repository licensing is not generalized to every upstream task artifact.

swe-marathon · has stage: SWE-Marathon’s paper describes proposal review, CI and LLM-assisted checks, pilot agent trials, adversarial exploit search and final human approval, revising and revalidating tasks with confirmed quality failures or exploits.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next12.swe-marathon.quality-pipeline.v2

  • These are the benchmark creators’ task-quality procedures, not ScienceToStartup peer receipts or proof that all future exploits are excluded.

swe-marathon · dataset size: The SWE-Marathon v1 paper describes 20 accepted project-scale tasks authored by 11 contributors across library reproduction, product cloning, ML engineering and algorithmic optimization.

  • The captured Refresh fork’s literal Markdown task rows 19–37 enumerate 19 tasks, while the creator paper describes 20. These are different historical scopes of one retained family; the earlier inherited 18-task note is not reused as an observed count.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

swe-marathon · benchmark task: SWE-Marathon tasks use Harbor instructions, Dockerized starter environments, development feedback, hidden verifiers, held-out human-written solution oracles and wall-clock limits, with final scoring based on the submitted container state.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next12.swe-marathon.task-format.v3

  • Visible feedback differs from stricter hidden final checks; some tasks omit visible tests.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

swe-marathon · evaluates: The SWE-Marathon paper’s reported protocol uses five trials for each of 13 agent-model configurations across 20 tasks, yielding 1,300 trajectories, and defines headline pass@1 as the fraction passing the task verifier.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next12.swe-marathon.trial-protocol.v2

  • The paper discloses expensive runs, seed variance, a single execution backend and unmeasured exploit false negatives. No new trial, ranking or successful exploit audit is claimed.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

swe-marathon · evaluates: SWE-Marathon combines task-specific tests, behavioral parity, performance gates, replay, integrity checks and—in selected product tasks—a browser-based rubric stage whose evidence is scored by a separate judge.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next12.swe-marathon.verification-design.v2

  • The appendix makes the S3-console UX stage optional while other named product tasks require both stages; no universal all-tasks UI requirement is inferred.
  • Verifier families are scoring mechanisms, not new logical benchmark families.
